blocks.text: Can Foreigners Buy Farmland in BC? Fraser Valley Rules

parts.t: Rules accurate as of October 18, 2026, and they can change. This is general information only, not legal or tax advice. Please speak to a BC real estate lawyer and an accountant before you buy.

Can people who are not Canadian citizens or permanent residents buy farmland in BC? Yes. BC does not limit who can own farmland, including land in the Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR). But other rules can still apply to a farm or acreage with a house on it, and some of them depend on where the property is. Here is how they fit together for buyers in the Fraser Valley.
BC does not restrict who can own farmland. The ALR controls how land is used, and those limits apply to every owner.
It covers a house of up to three units inside a census area. Vacant land is not covered. Under current law it ends on January 1, 2027, and Ottawa has not said what comes next.
It applies in Metro Vancouver and the Fraser Valley Regional District, and BC lists no end date. On farm-class land it is charged on the house plus 0.5 hectares of land.
For foreign owners it is 3% in 2026 and 4% from 2027, on covered residential property.
BC held a provincial election on October 24, 2026, and a new government can change the rules.

BC has no rule that stops a non-Canadian from owning farmland. In its response to a 2024 municipal resolution, the Ministry of Agriculture and Food said BC protects farmland through the Agricultural Land Commission Act and the ALR, “rather than through controlling ownership” (
That is not the whole story for a farm with a house. Four sets of rules can matter, and each one works differently.

blocks.text: The four sets of rules at a glance

parts.t: Set by the Government of Canada. It can stop a purchase of a covered home in a census area. Breaking it can mean a fine of up to $10,000. Under current law it ends January 1, 2027, unless Ottawa acts.
Set by BC. It cannot stop a purchase. It adds 20% of the value of the residential part. BC lists no end date.
Set by BC. It cannot stop a purchase. It is a yearly tax: 3% in 2026 and 4% from 2027 for foreign owners. It does not end in 2027, and the foreign-owner rate rises.
Set by BC (Agricultural Land Commission). They limit how land is used, not who owns it, so they cannot stop a purchase. Applications may be needed for some uses. They do not end in 2027.

blocks.text: 1. The federal home-buying ban: what it covers on a farm

parts.t: Prohibition on the Purchase of Residential Property by Non-Canadians Act

has been in force since January 1, 2023. It applies to anyone who is not a Canadian citizen, a person registered under the Indian Act, or a permanent resident. It also applies to foreign corporations and to some Canadian corporations that a non-Canadian controls.

That means a detached house or similar building with no more than three dwelling units, plus the land “reasonably necessary” for living in it. Semi-detached homes, rowhouses and condo units are covered too.
It only applies in census areas.
A census area is Statistics Canada’s term for a larger city and its surrounding communities. Property outside every census metropolitan area and census agglomeration is not covered (
CMHC says that has been the case since March 27, 2023 (
CMHC says ordinary repairs, renovations and remodels are not “development.”
Examples are a non-Canadian buying with a spouse or common-law partner who is a citizen or permanent resident, and some work-permit and student-permit holders who meet set conditions.

A non-Canadian who breaks the rule can be fined up to $10,000, and so can anyone who knowingly helps. A court can also order the home sold, and the non-Canadian would receive no more than the purchase price. The sale itself stays valid.
The Act covers the house and the land “reasonably necessary” for using it as a home. Whether that reaches a whole large farm parcel is a question for your lawyer, so please do not assume.

blocks.text: 2. BC’s 20% foreign buyer tax: what it is charged on

parts.t: of 20% on foreign nationals, foreign corporations and taxable trustees who buy residential property in the Capital, Fraser Valley, Metro Vancouver, Central Okanagan and Nanaimo regional districts. It is charged on the fair market value of the buyer’s share of the property.
On a farm, the tax applies only to the residential part. BC’s page sets out three cases:
If the whole property is classed as residential (class 1) by BC Assessment, the tax applies to the entire value.
If BC Assessment classes it as farm land because of an owner’s dwelling or a farmer’s dwelling, the tax applies to the value of the house plus 0.5 hectares (about 1.2 acres) of land.
If it is a mixed-class property, the tax applies to the residential part only.

Some exemptions exist, for example for a confirmed BC Provincial Nominee buying a principal residence (it can be claimed once). This tax is separate from the federal ban, and the BC page lists no end date. Ask for the property’s BC Assessment class before you write an offer.

blocks.text: 3. The Speculation and Vacancy Tax on a farm house

parts.t: (SVT) is a yearly tax on residential property in listed areas. Those areas include the municipalities in Metro Vancouver (including both Langleys, Surrey, Delta, Maple Ridge and Pitt Meadows), plus Abbotsford, Chilliwack and Mission (

are charged on the property’s assessed value. For 2026 the rate is 3% for foreign owners and untaxed worldwide earners, and 1% for Canadian citizens and permanent residents who are not untaxed worldwide earners. From January 1, 2027 the rates are 4% and 1%. Owners in taxable areas file a declaration each year by March 31, and exemptions such as a principal residence can apply.
Farms are treated differently. Under the

A house classed as residential on farm land is included, other than farm outbuildings, and property assessed at $150,000 or less is excluded. That is my plain-language reading, so ask your accountant how it applies to a specific property.

blocks.text: If you are buying farmland or acreage

parts.t: Talk to a BC real estate lawyer first about your own status and which rules apply to you.
Check whether the address is in a census area, using CMHC’s lookup.
Ask for the BC Assessment class (farm or residential). It affects the 20% tax and the SVT.
Check the ALR map, the home-size limits, the additional-home rules and local bylaws.
Ask your accountant about the SVT declaration and any other tax that could apply.

blocks.text: If you are selling a farm or acreage

parts.t: None of these rules changes how the ALR applies to your land. Price it for the buyers who are in the market today, and keep your lawyer involved when an offer comes with questions about the buyer’s legal status or financing.
Can foreigners buy farmland in BC?
Yes. BC does not limit who can own farmland, including ALR land. But the federal ban can apply to a house in a census area, the 20% tax and the SVT can apply, and ALR use rules apply to everyone.
Does the foreign buyer ban in BC apply to vacant farm land?
No. The federal ban has not covered vacant land since March 27, 2023. A house on the land can be covered if the property is in a census area.
Is the federal foreign buyer ban ending?
Under current law it is repealed on January 1, 2027. As of October 26, 2026, Ottawa has not announced a decision. BC’s 20% tax and the SVT are separate and do not end on that date.
Are there ALR non-resident ownership limits?
No. The ALR regulates how land is used, not who owns it. Limits such as the home-size rules apply to every owner.
Does the 20% foreign buyer tax apply to a whole farm?
Only to the residential part. On land classed as farm because of an owner’s or farmer’s dwelling, it applies to the house plus 0.5 hectares of land.
